# Ida Ashdown

## Overview

- **Age:** 10 years old  <sub>[v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** Juneford  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>

## Appearance

Ida has a delicate, small face, a pale complexion, and a slim, fragile build. She has straight, limp black hair without curls, which she wears in plaits, and large, deep-blue eyes that have a slanted, longing, and slightly sad expression. Her lips have a habit of parting above her small ivory teeth.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c4 P14](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0014), [v5 c4 P28](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0028), [v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c14 P17](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0017), [v5 c14 P19](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0019)_

## Personality

Ida is a quiet, sensitive, and deeply affectionate girl who is eager to do what is right. She is thoughtful, imaginative, and easily moved to tears by the suffering of others or by her own fears. Extremely shy and prone to worry, she often feels a troubling sense of responsibility for her family's reputation and household conditions, taking burdens onto her small shoulders. Despite her timid nature, she is capable of desperate bravery when motivated by her deep love for her father or her desire to protect someone else.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c4 P26](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0026), [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c5 P84](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0084), [v5 c9 P8](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0008), [v5 c9 P13](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0013), [v5 c10 P13](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0013)_

## History

Ida is the daughter of the Reverend John Knox Ashdown and lived in Juneford before moving to the Glen St. Agnes manse with her family. Growing up without a mother, she often feels a quiet ache of longing for her mother's memory and worries about her family's disorganized household. When an escaped orphan named Mary Stubbs seeks refuge in their barn, Ida offers her food, comfort, and a place to sleep in the manse attic. In an effort to stop public gossip about her family, she joins her siblings in forming a 'Good-Conduct Club' to self-punish their misdeeds. During one such punishment—a strict day-long fast—Ida passes out during a church service from lack of nourishment. Later, overhearing her father's deep sorrow and believing he needs a companion, Ida bravely walks to the house on the hill to personally ask Clementine Ainslie to marry him. Clementine reassures her, promises to be a friend rather than a cruel stepmother, and gives her a letter for her father, bringing about their reconciliation and eventual marriage.
